question: Sodium, carbon and oxygen elements are present in Washing Soda. Select the INCORRECT symbol of these elements.
solution:
The correct answer is __**SO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Washing Soda** is a chemical compound with the formula **Na₂CO₃.10H₂O**, which is chemically known as **Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate**.
 
• The elements that constitute washing soda are **Sodium**, **Carbon**, **Oxygen**, and **Hydrogen**.
 
• The symbol for **Sodium** is **Na**. This is derived from its **Latin** name, **Natrium**. *Hence, the symbol given in option 4 is correct.*
 
• The symbol for **Carbon** is **C**. It is a non-metallic element belonging to **Group 14** of the **Periodic Table**. *Hence, the symbol given in option 2 is correct.*
 
• The symbol for **Oxygen** is **O**. It is a highly reactive non-metal and oxidizing agent. *Hence, the symbol given in option 1 is correct.*
 
• The symbol **SO** is not an elemental symbol. **S** represents **Sulfur** and **O** represents **Oxygen**. Together they represent **Sulfur Monoxide**, which is not an element present in the standard chemical description of individual symbols for washing soda's components. ***Hence, option 3 is the incorrect symbol.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Composition:** **Washing Soda** contains **two atoms** of **Sodium**, **one atom** of **Carbon**, and **three atoms** of **Oxygen** in its anhydrous form (**Soda Ash**), along with **ten molecules** of **water of crystallization**.
 
• **Production:** It is predominantly manufactured using the **Solvay Process** (also known as the **ammonia-soda process**), which uses **Sodium Chloride**, **Ammonia**, and **Limestone** as raw materials.
 
• **Physical Properties:** It is a **white**, **crystalline** solid that is **soluble in water**. It undergoes **efflorescence**, where it loses water molecules when exposed to dry air to become **Sodium Carbonate Monohydrate**.
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• It is extensively used in **glass**, **soap**, and **paper** industries.
 
• It is used for **removing the permanent hardness of water**.
 
• It serves as a **cleansing agent** for domestic purposes and as a **laboratory reagent**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Details:**
 
 
• **Sodium (Na)**: Atomic number **11**, located in **Period 3**.
 
• **Carbon (C)**: Atomic number **6**, located in **Period 2**.
 
• **Oxygen (O)**: Atomic number **8**, located in **Period 2**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Differentiation:** It is important to distinguish **Washing Soda** from **Baking Soda**. While Washing Soda is **Sodium Carbonate** (**Na₂CO₃**), Baking Soda is **Sodium Bicarbonate** (**NaHCO₃**).
 
• **Nature:** **Sodium Carbonate** is a **basic salt** because it is formed by the reaction of a **strong base** (Sodium Hydroxide) and a **weak acid** (Carbonic Acid).
 
• **Historical Context:** Historically, it was extracted from the ashes of plants growing in sodium-rich soils, which is why the anhydrous form is still commonly referred to as **Soda Ash**.
